spans.text: ...At the Griffin defense line.
Doesn't look like cover's an issue anymore. How's the ammo at our fallback position?
The drone just dropped it off!
Will Military units really be coming our way?
Hehe...wouldn't THAT be nice? Chances to have fun like this don't come by often.
Besides, I still haven't settled the score with them from last time!
But we can't possibly bring down Military armored units with just our firepower, right?
Even their regular infantry models are hard to destroy once they're some distance away from us.
The Boss has a plan.
Squad B3, do you read me?
Ehh?! Is the enemy here already?
Relax, Gr MP5. Just asking for a routine report about the situation on your end.
You scared me to death...
We've planted the explosives behind the defense line, but is it really okay to booby trap our route of retreat?
The Boss has a plan.
Squads B4 and B5, what about you?
We're fine too!
Nothing out of the ordinary with B5.
Aren't these regular check-ins too frequent?
B4's prepped and ready to go!
Heehee, come, you enemies, come and die!
Thompson's worried about whether the enemy has secretly wiped out our forward listening posts. Besides, it's not like you're the one in charge of comms.
True, but you heard P7 just now, right? Don't tell me she's got her pranks ready to go?
Trust her this once. P7 doesn't mess around too much when it comes to actual combat.
I hope so, given the circumstances.
Wait a minute... Did you say "too much"?
Does it matter? At most we'll just wake up in an unfamiliar repair tank.
Are you sure we'll have a chance to wake up at all?
We will. I believe in the Commander.
Oh yes, where did STEN and that tomato go?
There are still a few houses to the northwest that haven't been cleared yet. They've gone up there to scout and lay a few traps while they're there.
I hope they don't blow themselves up before the fighting starts...
As the new Team Palette, we can't bring shame to our former leader.
Should we verify their positions?
Right, contact them.
B5-1 hailing B5-2.
What's your situation? Why are you taking so long?
Oh, it's 92.
We've finished planting mines at the designated location.
So why haven't you come back yet?
That's because...
Miss Negev asked us to help her out.
C3 hailing B5.
This is Negev, sorry for borrowing some of your people.
So it was Squad Negev. Don't sweat it, boss them around as much as you want.
Thank you very much. We'll send them back once we've finished digging in here.
How's the moving going?
It's...so...heavy...
Don't you usually use a machine gun? Why are you so weak?
Why don't...you try...carrying several dozen sandbags at once... (Pants)
Quit whining. If our position gets overrun, your flanks will be completely exposed. So please help us out. Miss Tomato.
Don't call me Tomato!
I'm terribly sorry about this, but the Commander wants the machine gun nests to be as secure as possible.
It's alright; after all, we ought to be helping each other out at times like these, am I right, Miss Tomato?
At least call me Mademoiselle Tomate... Argh, my arms are falling off...
A few more sandbags and it'll be over. Come on, hang in there.
This is the first line of defense, so we need to hold the enemy at bay and keep them from passing through.
So we're on the outermost edge of the defensive line? I saw a bunch of Dolls run outside just now.
They're probably recon teams. The Military's drawing closer, and the Commander needs to know the enemy's movements.
Still, they've been out for a while. I wonder how they're doing.
G1 hailing G5, can you see our position?
G5 copies, we see you clearly from here.
Please cover our reconnaissance... The enemy seems to have dispatched scout units as well, and they're headed our way.
Received. I recommend you pull your team back a little; your current position is very dangerous.
Understood, but we'll be able to spot the hostile armored trains from here more quickly.
If we can take the initiative, we'll lose much fewer Dolls in the upcoming battle.
...Roger.
We'll do our best to cover you.
Wait...
What's the matter?
I did a scan and found a faint signal approaching this location. I think it's an autonomous force conducting armed recon.
We can't let them get close to our defense line, so let's wipe them out here.
I've synced the data to you.
Received. These numbers shouldn't pose a problem.
StG, have the rest of our teammates cover them as well.
Got it, I'm contacting them now.
G43, are you still at the resupply point?
I'm on my way back.
Change of plan. Proceed directly to firing point 3, we're moving the crossfire plan up.
Got it, I'm coming over now!
There's been a change of plan, MP41.
Oh, was that from Fräulein Kar?
She's at the shooting point, and she wants us to head over right away.
Er...does it have to be right now?
I wanted to write a report on the surrounding situation and send it to the Commander...
Forget the report, just remember to be a good spotter for me afterwards. We don't often get the chance to fight alongside Fräulein Kar!
Fine, fine, I got it... Plus, if you bite it, I can take over and help Fräulein Kar. Sounds good, right?
You shut that mouth of yours!
...Inside the command room on the train.
Looks like everyone's just about ready.
Yup, and I guess our opposition ought to be ready too.
Dandelion, have our Dolls been backed up?
All back-ups are complete. However, I will not be able to perform real-time neural backups for destroyed Dolls once the fighting starts. The data load is too great.
I'm grateful enough for pre-battle backups.
...That way, even if we get blown to bits, these girls will all survive as long as you or M4 make it.
That is true, in theory.
However, saying that sort of thing will only needlessly increase the stress on all of you. For instance, I can already sense that Miss Kalina is very much on edge.
Er...
Kalina... I'm sorry.
It's fine, Commander, ahahaha... You've always been one for saying scary things, haven't you?
I hope they're just empty words, but I have a really bad feeling about this. Maybe the good luck we've had all this while is about to be used up.

I've collated the data from all the Dolls and analyzed the battle situation, which I've projected on the main monitor in the command room. It shows the current disposition of our forces and predictions of enemy movements. I hope this information will help ease the stress on you.
How did you do that...?
Usually we only get this kind of computational support at the base.

You can think of me as a top-of-the-line supercomputer system. Since you are the only commander in Griffin to enjoy such luxurious treatment, your existence can be considered to be on the 'cutting edge'.
Is it not funny?
I thought humorous utterances would help relieve stress. It would seem I will need to avoid such forms of humor in the future.
I appreciate your good intentions... But let's focus on the battle.
Bzzzz — a buzzer goes off.
What's happening?
Message from the recon team. The enemy armored trains have stopped moving and they have dispatched autonomous scouting forces, which are currently engaging the recon team.
The trains are now deploying ground forces, and both our left and right flanks each have two companies' worth of troops headed their way.
They're going to catch us in a pincer attack. Looks like the opposition isn't interested in fancy tactics; they're going to hit us with everything they have.
Are there any other movements?
Hang on... I've lost contact with them...
The HOCs have sent a report... The recon team is being bombarded.
The firefight just now exposed our listening post, and the enemy brought their train-based artillery to bear. Team G1, G3 and G7 have been destroyed.
Two teams from Group K were subjected to mortar bombardment while planting explosives along the railway, and they had no choice but to fall back to cover.
The echelons on the main line of defense are still in cover. Group B is requesting support from Group C.
Dammit...they're showing us no mercy at all...
Have everyone from Group G fall back. Keep the defense echelons in cover and don't let them expose themselves.
They'll bombard the defense line if they reveal themselves too soon.
Stick with Plan A for now.
The defense line on the Lahepere Bay front is being hit too!
The Doll echelons are taking cover on the other side of the slope!
Are they planning on a breakthrough there...
Meanwhile...
On the Military armored train.
Sitrep?

Our autonomous forces have encountered a Griffin listening post. It has been obliterated via fire support. The 52nd and 54th armored companies are deployed and the 14th infantry reconnaissance company is in position.
Autonomous companies C and D are performing final adjustments and will be ready in five minutes.
Follow the plan and deploy our forces with mixed human and automaton composition. Also, beware of enemy hacking.
Griffin has prepared this choke point to block us. They have very few positions from which they can mount a defense, so sweep all those locations with cannonfire beforehand.
Understood.
Will our forces still be attacking in waves?
It's just a PMC. Can't we just crush them in one blow?
That PMC is just the velvet glove over a mailed fist. There's no telling where our true enemy is hiding. We must not fail this mission - we have to act cautiously.
Understood, sir.
Position all our armored forces on the north flank. I'm more worried about the Paldiski Base's coastal defense batteries than Griffin.
However, the fact that those cannons haven't started firing on us implies Griffin hasn't taken control of them yet.
Wasn't that base originally ours?
It used to be, but some bastard wrecked it.
Is that why we have no choice but to take it back?
Yes, we need to reclaim the base, as well as our soldier's honor, which has been trampled upon.
Yes, sir!
The PMC is still building up their defenses. When will we attack?
The troops are in high spirits and everyone is eager to make our enemies pay.
We will carry out any mission you give us, Captain.
I know, I feel the same as everyone else.
But we are soldiers, and so we must obey our orders.
It isn't time yet. Give them a taste of our wrath in the form of cannonfire.
